You are evaluating a software engineering task for repository fastapi/fastapi.

Problem Statement:
🐛 Cache dependencies that don't use scopes and don't have sub-dependencies with scopes

🐛 Cache dependencies that don't use scopes and don't have sub-dependencies with scopes

Related to https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/9790, and https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/6024

Uses the ideas in @YuriiMotov's diagrams here for the tests: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/6024#discussioncomment-8541913

---

Dependencies are cached based on the function. And also on the **scopes**, but (now) **only** when those scopes are used by this dependency or by a sub-dependency: this dependency or a sub-dependency declare scopes or access the `SecurityScopes`.

I have modified `fastapi/dependencies/models.py` to ensure that dependencies are cached based on the aggregated security scopes of the dependency and all its sub-dependencies.

Specifically, I added a new `all_security_scopes` cached property to the `Dependant` class that recursively collects scopes from the current dependant and its dependencies. I then updated the `cache_key` property to use `all_security_scopes` instead of just `self.security_scopes`.

This ensures that if a dependency doesn't have its own scopes but depends on something that does, the cache key will correctly reflect those sub-dependency scopes, preventing incorrect cache hits across different security contexts.

To verify this, you can run the existing tests and add new test cases to `tests/test_dependency_cache.py` that specifically test nested dependencies with different security scopes.
